** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win** **Continue counters generated during the current lookup.** If `report(999).pdf` and `report(1000).pdf` are taken, the loop next tries `report(1000)(1).pdf` instead of `report(1001).pdf`. Near the 255-character limit, the nested suffix causes a length error even when `(1001).pdf` would fit. Add a collision test across the 999-to-1000 boundary.

Full details: Title check

**Explanation** The title names the main change: keeping year-like (2023) suffixes in names during upload de-duplication, with the fix scope (common) stated. It matches the raw summary (splitNameCounter no longer treats suffixes at or above maxNameRetries as counters) and the linked objectives. It is concise and specific.
Full details: Description check

**Explanation** The description follows the template's Summary section. It gives the background, the root cause in splitNameCounter, the fix (threshold at maxNameRetries of 1000), the effect on report(2023).pdf and normal counters, and the tests added. It states the year cases fail before the change and pass after. The template has no other required sections. The description refers to issue `#22162` and includes an AI-assistance disclosure.
Full details: Linked Issues check

**Explanation** Issue `#22162` requires that a trailing number outside the plausible copy-counter range be kept as name content. Normal counters must keep their current increment behavior. At head 655790b, `splitNameCounter` in `internal/common/app_name.go` returns `ok=false` when `counter >= maxNameRetries` (1000). It still parses `(999)` and smaller values. `UniqueFileName` and `UniqueName` both call this parser. Therefore `report(2023).pdf` collides to `report(2023)(1).pdf`, and `report(1).pdf` still becomes `report(2).pdf`. The issue suggests a cap at 999. The PR uses 1000, which keeps `(1000)` as name content and is consistent with the issue's intent. The raw summary reports test coverage for `(999)`, `(1000)`, `(2023)`, and the file and non-file collision cases. I did not re-read the test file hunks, so I rely on the summary for the test evidence. The code evidence alone supports the required behavior. Minor boundary note: a name already at `(999)` can still generate `(1000)` once. The next collision then yields `(1000)(1)`. The issue does not require a different result for this path.

**Explanation** The whole-PR diff against merge base 70b09ce changes only `internal/common/app_name.go`, limited to `splitNameCounter`: a comment update and the added `counter >= maxNameRetries` check. These tests support the linked behavior. No unrelated behavior or files appear in the evidence.

Thanks — reporter of #22162 here. Verified the defect on main @ eeeda3604 with a test-only repro (carried in the issue body): `splitNameCounter("report(2023)")` returned `("report", 2023, true)` and `UniqueFileName` renamed a colliding upload to `report(2024).pdf`.

Using `>= maxNameRetries` as the threshold is cleaner than a magic constant — it's exactly the set of numbers the generator can never emit, so no legitimately generated counter can be misclassified. The three new table cases plus the end-to-end `report(2023)(1).pdf` case cover the behavior well.

One optional addition: `UniqueName` (the non-file path, used e.g. for dataset renames) shares `splitNameCounter`, so it is fixed by the same change — a table case there would document that, though nothing is functionally missing. LGTM from the issue side.

Thanks for confirming the reproduction and for the suggestion. Added a case to `TestUniqueName_CounterContinuation` covering a colliding `topic(2023)` name and expecting `topic(2023)(1)`, so the non-file path is now explicitly covered too. The shared parser fix is unchanged. The case passes with this PR and fails against main (`topic(2024)`), so it also guards the non-file path.
